## Problem

## Requirements

You are given a complete directed graph whose edge weights are all positive. Determine a node-simple path—one that never revisits a vertex—that yields the largest possible multiplication of its edge weights.

```python
def max_product_path(W, start):
```

The path must start at `start`, may end at any vertex, and may stop before visiting all vertices. Edge weights may be less than 1, equal to 1, or greater than 1. Return both the maximum product and the selected route.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Since edge weights are positive, longer paths tend to have larger products, but you must avoid cycles.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

This is a longest path problem in a DAG if you consider topological order, but the graph is complete, so you need to think about which vertices to visit.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The optimal path will visit vertices in decreasing order of some key, consider sorting vertices by weight and using dynamic programming.

</details>
